plain: The main money. Earned by selling resources, scanning life, and trading; spent on ships, slots, fuel and goods.
note: One of three currencies — don't confuse it with Nanites or Quicksilver; each is spent in different places.

plain: A secondary currency used to buy blueprints and upgrade modules.
note: Earn them by refining Salvaged Data or Runaway Mould, or by scrapping ships. Units can't buy most upgrade modules — nanites can.

plain: A cosmetic-only currency from the Nexus and some story steps.
note: Spends only at the Quicksilver vendor on decorations and customisations — never needed for actual progress.

plain: A machine that converts resources into other resources (e.g. Ferrite Dust into Pure Ferrite). Comes in portable, medium and large sizes.
note: The heart of money-making: many recipes multiply output, so a refiner often beats selling raw materials.

plain: A portable cooker. Combine up to three edible ingredients into food; valid combos give a product.
note: Needs no fuel or power, unlike the refiner. Cooked food sells well and is an easy nanite/units side-earner.

plain: A learned recipe that lets you craft a tech, product or base part.
note: Gained from story missions, the Anomaly, manufacturing facilities and Salvaged Data — you must learn it before you can build it.

plain: A item dug from Buried Technology, used to buy base/tech blueprints at a Construction Research Station.
note: Also refines into nanites. Find it by scanning for a Wi-Fi-like icon and digging with the Terrain Manipulator.

plain: The colour-coded metals (Copper, Cadmium, Emeril, Indium) found by star colour; refine into Chromatic Metal.
note: Higher-colour metals need better warp drives to reach but refine into far more Chromatic Metal.

plain: Your spacesuit — it holds your personal inventory, survival systems and worn technology.
note: Expanding its slots (station terminal + Drop Pods) is the single biggest early quality-of-life upgrade.

plain: Your handheld device: mining beam, scanner, terrain tool and weapon in one.
note: Comes in types (Pistol, Rifle, etc.) and classes C–S. You can own several and swap between them.

plain: Your spaceship for flight, space combat and interstellar travel.
note: You can own many and switch freely; each has its own inventory, class and type.

plain: A quality tier. C is lowest, S is best, with bigger stat bonuses and more slots as the class rises.
note: Class applies to ships, multi-tools, freighters and frigates. S-class costs the most but is worth saving for.

plain: The role of a ship: Fighter (combat), Hauler (storage), Explorer (warp range), Shuttle (balanced), Exotic (rare, always S-class), plus Solar, Interceptor and Living Ships.
note: Type sets the class bonus, so pick one that matches how you play.

plain: A huge capital ship that acts as a mobile base with big storage and a fleet command room.
note: Your first one can be free by defending a freighter under pirate attack. Not the same as a frigate.

plain: A mid-sized fleet ship you command from a freighter and send on automated expeditions.
note: Frigates earn units and items over real-world hours, even while you're offline — passive income once set up.

plain: The starship tech that lets you warp between star systems.
note: Upgrade drives (Cadmium/Emeril/Indium) unlock travel to higher-colour star systems.

plain: The fuel a Hyperdrive burns to warp. Crafted from Antimatter + Antimatter Housing.
note: Each cell fills about 20% of the tank, so keep several before long trips.

plain: A crafted ingredient (Chromatic Metal + Condensed Carbon) that goes into Warp Cells.
note: The story gives you the recipe; you can also buy it, but making it is far cheaper.

plain: Two ship systems: the Launch Thruster lifts you off a planet, the Pulse Engine zooms between points within a system.
note: Launch Thrusters use Di-hydrogen/launch fuel; the Pulse Engine uses Tritium from asteroids. Running dry strands you.

plain: Two survival meters. Hazard Protection shields you from weather/toxicity; Life Support keeps your suit running.
note: Recharge Hazard with Sodium and Life Support with Oxygen/Carbon; both refill instantly inside your ship.

plain: Your scanning view. Identifies resources, tags points of interest, and scans flora/fauna for units.
note: Also reveals deposit/hotspot locations and Buried Technology — use it constantly.

plain: A multi-tool attachment that digs, removes and adds terrain.
note: Needed to mine buried deposits and Salvaged Data, and to tunnel for shelter or bases.

plain: A slotted upgrade that boosts a ship/suit/tool stat. Bought with nanites or found.
note: Adjacency matters: place matching upgrades next to each other and the core tech for a bonus.

plain: Planetary vehicles (Roamer, Colossus, Nomad, Pilgrim, Minotaur, Nautilon submarine) for fast ground or underwater travel.
note: Built from a base or freighter Exocraft station; great for scanning hotspots and long surface hauls.

plain: The anchor you place to claim a build area and start a base.
note: Setting one up drips free building blueprints over time via its archive mission.

plain: A base box for stashing resources; contents are shared and accessible from any of your bases.
note: Items in storage (and your ship) are never lost on death — deposit valuables before risky trips.

plain: A base/station device for instant travel between your bases and visited space stations.
note: Build one early; it saves huge amounts of flying once you have several bases.

plain: A terminal (on the Anomaly, or buildable) that sells base-building blueprints for Salvaged Data.
note: This is where most storage, refiner, door and decoration plans come from.

plain: Automated harvesters placed on a hotspot to mine resources or gases continuously.
note: Need power (Solar Panels + Batteries or a Biofuel Reactor). The basis of passive resource/income farms.

plain: A placeable object that creates a manual save when you interact with it.
note: Handy because there's no "save and quit"; otherwise just hop out of your ship to save.

plain: A trade-focused amphibious species. Their systems specialise in Starship technology.
note: Good relations and their planets/stations make ship upgrades easier to find.

plain: A science-minded machine species that reveres the Atlas. Their systems specialise in Exosuit technology.
note: Visit Korvax space when hunting exosuit upgrades.

plain: A warrior species with a strict honour code and a hatred of Sentinels. Their systems specialise in Multi-Tool technology.
note: Best place to shop for multi-tool upgrades.

plain: Robotic enforcers that police planets and react if you over-mine or attack wildlife.
note: Provoking them escalates through drones, walkers and ships. Corrupted Sentinels on Dissonant worlds drop nanite-rich Tainted Metal.

plain: Rare wandering explorers — the same kind of being you play as.
note: Talking to them at stations advances a lore quest and can give useful rewards.

plain: A vast cosmic entity central to the main story and the nature of the universe.
note: The Atlas Path is one of the core questlines; its interfaces hand out story rewards.

plain: A travelling hub you can summon in space. Nada and Polo give missions and sell blueprints/upgrades; the Nexus offers multiplayer missions.
note: Visit early and often — the cheap nanite blueprints here accelerate everything.

plain: The buy/sell screen at stations, trading posts and freighters.
note: Prices vary by system and demand; selling lots of one item crashes its local price.

plain: A located concentration of a resource (mineral, gas or power) found with the multi-tool's Survey Device.
note: Build the matching Extractor on a hotspot for steady passive resources.

plain: Two save types: an autosave (the game makes periodically and on key events) and a Restore Point (made when you exit your ship).
note: On reload you may be asked which to load — pick the more recent one.

plain: Discoveries are the planets, systems and life you scan and can name; Milestones track your overall progress and standings.
note: Uploading discoveries pays units and is safe to do whenever you have a connection.
